title: SLO-driven pool sizing and safety margins — hosted API forecast
summary: Working notes for aligning hosted API GPU pool sizing to SLO classes, introducing a KV-hit-adjusted tokens/sec metric, and defining safety multipliers for operational headroom across regions.
body:
Purpose:
This document captures the reasoning and working numbers for sizing GPU pools in the Hosted API fleet such that capacity maps directly to customer SLO classes (Gold/Silver/Bronze). It intentionally focuses on SLO-driven headroom (not just cost-minimization) and introduces a simple correction factor for prefix/KV cache effects (KV-hit-adjusted tokens/sec).

Scope and audience:
- Audience: Infra on-call, capacity planning, SRE, product (hosted-api), solutions eng.
- Scope: Global hosted API (public endpoints). Regional splits for US-W, US-E, EU, APAC. Model classes: small generation (~7B), medium (~13–30B), large (~70B), and embedding-only. Quantization & kernel mix assumed per region based on telemetry.

Key assumptions (baseline):
- Baseline peak window = 30-minute top QPS per day (derived from last 6 months rolling peaks).
- Avg tokens per request (TPR) by class: small=120, medium=210, large=380, embedding=32.
- KV cache effective hit ratio (prefix caching) baseline: 18% overall (varies by product). We adjust tokens/sec capacity by (1 - KV_hit) to get KV-hit-adjusted tokens/sec demand.
- Representative GPU sustained tokens/sec (inference throughput) per device (avg operating config):
  - H100-80GB (FP16/AMP): 4,200 tokens/sec (large models), 8,500 tokens/sec (small models, higher batch efficiency)
  - A100-80GB (FP16): 3,000 tokens/sec (large), 6,000 tokens/sec (small)
  - T4-like/Low-end for embeddings: 18,000 tokens/sec (embedding workloads measured separately)
- Target sustained utilization per GPU for planned capacity (not ephemeral): 72% for Gold SLA, 78% for Silver, 85% for Bronze. We accept lower utilization for higher SLO to preserve tail latency.

New metric: KV-hit-adjusted tokens/sec
- Definition: observed tokens/sec demand * (1 - KV_hit_ratio). Rationale: prefix cache removes repeated tokens from the expensive token-processing path; we therefore size physical token throughput on the KV-miss-adjusted quantity.
- Example: raw peak tokens/sec = 1,000,000; KV_hit=0.18 -> adjusted demand = 820,000 tokens/sec.

Sizing methodology (stepwise):
1) Compute region-level raw peak tokens/sec from telemetry (QPS * TPR distribution over 30m peak).
2) Apply KV-hit adjustment.
3) Split by model class using observed mix (percent of requests by model family).
4) For each class, divide adjusted tokens/sec by the per-GPU tokens/sec for that model & GPU family to get required GPUs.
5) Apply SLO-driven utilization target and safety multiplier by SLA class to compute final reserved pool size.

Safety multipliers (recommended):
- Gold (99.95 latency SLO): 1.35 (35% safety headroom above adjusted steady-state need)
- Silver (99.9): 1.20
- Bronze (best-effort): 1.05
Rationale: gold customers must survive sudden bursts and cold-cache tail events; the extra headroom translates to lower p95/p99 latency and reduced fallback frequency.

Representative worked example (US-W, evening peak):
- Observed peak QPS mix at peak 18:00 PST: total QPS = 7,400 (small 45%, medium 30%, large 20%, embeddings 5%)
- Using TPRs above -> raw peak tokens/sec = QPS * TPR-weighted-average
  - Weighted TPR = 0.45*120 + 0.30*210 + 0.20*380 + 0.05*32 = 166.6 tokens/request
  - raw tokens/sec = 7,400 * 166.6 = 1,232,000 tokens/sec
- KV-hit-adjusted = 1,232,000 * (1 - 0.18) = 1,010,240 tokens/sec
- Split by model class (tokens contribution):
  - small: 0.45 * 1,010,240 = 454,608 tokens/sec -> on H100 small-efficiency 8,500 t/s per GPU -> 53.5 GPUs -> rounded 54 GPUs
  - medium: 0.30 * 1,010,240 = 303,072 -> assume medium uses H100 medium-efficiency 6,000 t/s -> 50.5 -> 51 GPUs
  - large: 0.20 * 1,010,240 = 202,048 -> H100 large-efficiency 4,200 t/s -> 48.1 -> 49 GPUs
  - embeddings: 0.05 * 1,010,240 = 50,512 -> on T4-pool 18,000 t/s -> 2.8 -> 3 GPUs
- Raw required GPUs (rounded) = 157 GPUs (H100-equivalent mix + 3 T4).
- Apply utilization target and Gold safety multiplier (assume 60% of this regional traffic is Gold):
  - Gold portion: 0.60 * 157 = 94.2 -> require 94.2 * (1 / 0.72 utilization) * 1.35 safety = 176 GPUs reserved for Gold (rounded)
  - Silver portion: 0.30 * 157 = 47.1 -> 47.1 * (1/0.78) * 1.20 = 72 GPUs
  - Bronze portion: 0.10 * 157 = 15.7 -> 15.7 * (1/0.85) * 1.05 = 19 GPUs
- Final regional reserved pool (US-W example) = 176 + 72 + 19 = 267 GPUs (H100-equivalent) + 3 T4 for embeddings.

Notes on rounding and pooling efficiency:
- We recommend pooling across SLA classes where latency SLOs allow: i.e., Silver+Bronze can share a flexible pool with preemption by Gold. The math above seeds reserved capacity by SLA to support isolation.
- When converting heterogeneous hardware (A100 / H100) we use a common normalization to 'H100-equivalent tokens/sec' to avoid overprovisioning.

Prewarm & cold-pool strategy (operational):
- Maintain a warm pool sized to cover 60% of Gold day-to-day peak; remaining Gold headroom is covered by quick warm-ups + pre-warmed standby racks (cold-pool) that can be ramped in 90–180s.
- Cold-pool composition: 10% of active pool as cold-warm instances (preloaded container but not assigned cache) and 5% as instant-warm reserved (hot racks with network prepped).
- Autoscaling preference: prefer horizontal scaling within same region/GPU family; cross-region failover only when regional capacity exhausted or targeted latency tradeoff acceptable.

Failure & fallback policies tied to headroom tiers:
- If Gold pool utilization > 88% for >3m: trigger soft-throttle on non-critical features + route new low-priority requests to Bronze fallback model (smaller model variant).
- If utilization climbs >95% persistently: trigger cross-region spill to adjacent region with capacity and lower SLOs, notify on-call and product.

Cost impact (rough):
- Example US-W baseline reserved increase from 157 -> 267 GPUs (H100-equivalent) in the worked example. If H100 hourly cost ~$5.00 (market varies), incremental monthly cost delta = (267 - 157) * 24 * 30 * $5 = $1,632,000/month.
- Tradeoff: reduces Gold latency P99 and decreases fallback incidence (cost versus user-facing quality).

Operational actions (next 30 days):
- [Infra] Pull 3-month rolling peak windows per region with model-family splits and KV-hit time series (owner: Elliot) - due 2026-03-18.
- [SRE] Run a synthetic 60-minute steady-burst test at 1.25x current observed peak to validate autoscaler step latency (owner: Sofia) - due 2026-03-22.
- [Product] Confirm SLA bucket percentages by customer tier for budgeting (owner: Priya) - due 2026-03-12.
- [Finance] Provide delta cost scenarios for H100 vs A100 mixes given preferred pool sizes (owner: Finance lead) - due 2026-03-25.

Open questions and risks:
- KV-hit volatility: many products show KV-hit swings during campaigns; we need per-product correction factors rather than global 18%.
- Model migration impact: migrating large customers to a quantized variant can change per-GPU tokens/sec materially; include a migration buffer.
- Prewarm time variance: some models still have 2–3x slower cold-starts on new kernels. Does that require larger hot-rack reservation?

Appendix: quick projection CSV (region,raw_tokens_s,kv_adjusted_tps,estimated_gpus_before_safety,final_reserved_gpus)

US-E,870000,713400,112,190

Concluding note:
This doc is intended as a working artifact: numbers are illustrative and depend on the telemetry pull. Use the stepwise method here to derive conservative reserved pools aligned to SLOs. Feedback welcome in-thread; once we converge we will create a canonical sheet with live links to telemetry and a parametric calculator for planners.
